---
title: "CanadaLogin Errors"
author: "EDCP Data and Research Team"  # colin.douglas@cds-snc.ca
slug: errors
format:
  dashboard:
    # Written by the setup chunk at render time
    include-before-body: page-header.html
    include-after-body:
      - analytics-tag.html # see _analytics.qmd
      # Bootstrap tooltips on codes and feature names. A native title tooltip is slow, and
      # some browsers and previews never show it. On body, so no card clips it.
      - text: |
          <script>
          window.addEventListener("load", () => {
            document.querySelectorAll(".hover-tip[title]").forEach((el) => {
              new bootstrap.Tooltip(el, { container: "body", placement: "top" });
            });
          });
          </script>
params:
  ga_page_title: "Errors Dashboard"
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false

# Thresholds ------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Every number that decides what the page shows.
thresholds <- list(
  # Flagged when a week's rate is at least `ratio` times the median of the
  # `history_weeks` before it, on at least `min_events` events.
  ratio = 2,
  min_events = 50,
  history_weeks = 4L,
  # Weeks in each trend line, ending with the report week.
  trend_weeks = 12L,
  # Longest span of the charts; until there is that much data, all of it.
  chart_weeks = 26L,
  # New and returning codes are listed from this many events in the week.
  new_min_events = 5L,
  # Every other code is listed from this many events in the week.
  list_min_events = 20L,
  # Codes named for each feature.
  feature_codes = 3L,
  # Preflight: no day may have fewer sessions than this share of the median day.
  sessions_floor = 0.2
)

# Setup -----------------------------------------------------------------------

# The working directory is this folder; the shared layer is two levels up.
source("../../common/setup.R")

source("R/metrics.R")
source("R/preflight.R")

con <- connect_athena()

# A failed check adds a banner. See R/preflight.R.
preflight <- run_preflight_safety_check(con, thresholds)
write_preflight_status(preflight)

week <- report_week(toronto_today())
from <- min(weeks_needed(week, thresholds),
            week$start - 7L * (thresholds$chart_weeks - 1L))

errors <- dplyr::filter(error_rows(con, from), day <= week$end)
sessions <- dplyr::filter(session_days(con, from), day <= week$end)

# One message per code, for the tooltips. From the private catalogue in the
# publishing repo; with no file, codes have no tooltip.
messages <- code_messages(private_data("error-codes.yml", read = yaml::read_yaml))

features <- feature_table(errors, sessions, week, thresholds, messages)
codes <- code_table(errors, sessions, week, thresholds)
overall <- overall_rate(errors, sessions, week, thresholds)
unlabelled <- unlabelled_forms(dplyr::filter(errors, day >= week$start))
overall_weeks <- chart_weeks(errors, sessions, week, thresholds)
feature_weeks <- chart_weeks(errors, sessions, week, thresholds, by_feature = TRUE)

page_header <- "page-header.html"

write_preflight_banner(preflight, page_header)

cat(
  c(
    '<div class="page-strip">',
    # Through the report week's Sunday: days after it are not a whole week yet.
    glue("  <p><strong>Data through {format_long_date(week$end)}.</strong> ",
         "Internal to Enterprise Digital Credentials, not for public ",
         "consumption.</p>"),
    "</div>"
  ),
  file = page_header, sep = "\n", append = TRUE
)

# Presentation ---------------------------------------------------------------

# Mirrors _theme.scss: brand red only for what was flagged.
ink <- list(flag = "#AB2328", trend = "#952535", quiet = "#5C6670")

trend_label <- "Errors per 1,000 sessions, weekly"
against_label <- glue("Against the {thresholds$history_weeks} weeks before")

table_options <- function(gt_table) {
  tab_options(gt_table, table.width = pct(100), table.font.size = px(14),
              data_row.padding = px(3), table.border.top.style = "none",
              column_labels.font.weight = "bold")
}

# The trend as one column per week, for cols_nanoplot().
spread_trend <- function(rows) {
  weeks <- purrr::map(rows$trend, \(x) {
    stats::setNames(as.list(x), sprintf("w%02d", seq_along(x)))
  })
  dplyr::bind_cols(dplyr::select(rows, -trend), dplyr::bind_rows(weeks))
}

# The shared columns of both tables: events, rate, change and trend. The change
# is coloured by colour_changes(), where fewer errors is good; flagged, new and
# returning rows are bold.
rate_columns <- function(gt_table) {
  gt_table |>
    fmt_number(events, decimals = 0) |>
    cols_nanoplot(
      columns = dplyr::starts_with("w"),
      plot_type = "bar",
      expand_y = 0,
      new_col_name = "trend",
      new_col_label = trend_label,
      options = nanoplot_options(
        data_bar_fill_color = ink$trend,
        data_bar_stroke_color = ink$trend,
        show_data_points = FALSE,
        # The values shown on hover, formatted like every other rate.
        y_val_fmt_fn = fmt_rate,
        y_axis_fmt_fn = fmt_rate
      )
    ) |>
    colour_changes("against", "verdict") |>
    tab_style(cell_text(weight = "bold"),
              cells_body(columns = against, rows = flagged | new)) |>
    cols_hide(c(flagged, new, verdict)) |>
    cols_align("right", columns = c(events, rate, against)) |>
    cols_align("center", columns = trend)
}

feature_gt <- function(rows) {
  rows |>
    dplyr::transmute(feature = feature_html(feature), events, rate = fmt_rate(rate),
                     against = fmt_against(change, new, returning, typical,
                                           events),
                     trend, codes, flagged, new,
                     verdict = error_verdict(change, new, typical, events)) |>
    spread_trend() |>
    gt() |>
    rate_columns() |>
    fmt_passthrough(c(feature, codes), escape = FALSE) |>
    cols_move(codes, after = trend) |>
    # styles.css lets the first two columns wrap; feature names stay whole.
    tab_style(cell_text(whitespace = "nowrap"), cells_body(columns = feature)) |>
    cols_width(feature ~ pct(17), events ~ pct(8), rate ~ pct(10),
               against ~ pct(14), trend ~ pct(21), codes ~ pct(30)) |>
    cols_label(feature = "Feature", events = "Errors",
               rate = "Per 1,000 sessions", against = against_label,
               codes = "Top codes this week") |>
    table_options()
}

code_gt <- function(rows) {
  rows |>
    dplyr::transmute(code = code_html(error_code, messages), feature, events,
                     rate = fmt_rate(rate),
                     against = fmt_against(change, new, returning, typical,
                                           events),
                     trend, flagged, new,
                     verdict = error_verdict(change, new, typical, events)) |>
    spread_trend() |>
    gt() |>
    rate_columns() |>
    fmt_passthrough(code, escape = FALSE) |>
    cols_label(code = "Code", feature = "Mostly on", events = "Errors",
               rate = "Per 1,000 sessions", against = against_label) |>
    cols_width(code ~ pct(16), feature ~ pct(20), trend ~ pct(24)) |>
    table_options()
}

# Charts ---------------------------------------------------------------------

# Weekly points sit on the Sunday each week ends.
week_end_of <- function(monday) monday + 6L

brand_figure <- function(p) {
  add_cds_logo(
    add_watermark(p, report_name = "CanadaLogin Errors", date = week$end),
    height = 0.09
  )
}

week_scale <- function() {
  scale_x_date(labels = format_short_date,
               expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.04)))
}

rate_scale <- function() {
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, NA),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08)))
}

# All errors each week, the report week marked and labelled with its rate.
overall_chart <- function(rows) {
  latest <- dplyr::filter(rows, week == max(week))
  p <- ggplot(rows, aes(week_end_of(week), rate)) +
    geom_line(colour = ink$trend, linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(data = latest, colour = ink$trend, size = 2.6) +
    geom_text(data = latest, aes(label = fmt_rate(rate)), vjust = -1.1,
              size = 3.6, colour = "grey20") +
    week_scale() +
    rate_scale() +
    theme_cds() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
    labs(x = "Week ending", y = "Errors per 1,000 sessions",
         title = "All errors per 1,000 sessions, by week")
  brand_figure(p)
}

# One panel per feature, busiest this week first, all on one scale so the
# panels compare: a tall panel is a big share of errors. One colour, since
# position and the panel title already name each feature.
feature_chart <- function(rows, features) {
  rows <- dplyr::mutate(rows, key = factor(key, levels = features$feature))
  p <- ggplot(rows, aes(week_end_of(week), rate)) +
    geom_area(fill = ink$trend, alpha = 0.15) +
    geom_line(colour = ink$trend, linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~key, ncol = 3) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
    rate_scale() +
    theme_cds() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold")) +
    labs(x = "Week ending", y = "Errors per 1,000 sessions",
         title = "Errors per 1,000 sessions by feature, by week")
  brand_figure(p)
}

overall_alt <- glue(
  "Line chart of all errors per 1,000 sessions each week, for the ",
  "{nrow(overall_weeks)} weeks ending ",
  "{format_long_date(week_end_of(min(overall_weeks$week)))} ",
  "to {format_long_date(week$end)}. The latest week is ",
  "{fmt_rate(overall$rate)}, against a median of {fmt_rate(overall$typical)} ",
  "over the {thresholds$history_weeks} weeks before."
)

feature_alt <- glue(
  "Small multiple line charts of errors per 1,000 sessions each week, one ",
  "panel per feature, all on the same scale, busiest first. This week: ",
  "{glue_collapse(glue('{features$feature} {fmt_rate(features$rate)}'), sep = ', ')}."
)

# A value box's third line naming what was flagged. It always leads with
# words: a line that is a single code would lose its paragraph.
flag_line <- function(names) {
  if (length(names) == 0) return("None at twice the usual rate")
  glue("At twice the usual rate: {glue_collapse(names, sep = ', ', last = ' and ')}")
}

flagged_features <- flag_line(features$feature[features$flagged])

# One feature's rate and change, for its value box; dashes if it had no errors
# in the weeks the page reads.
feature_box <- function(name) {
  row <- dplyr::filter(features, feature == name)
  if (nrow(row) == 0) return(list(rate = "-", change = "-"))
  list(rate = nbsp(fmt_rate(row$rate)),
       change = change_html(row$change, good = "down"))
}

sign_in_box <- feature_box("Sign in")
sign_up_box <- feature_box("Sign up")
flagged_codes <- flag_line(codes$error_code[codes$flagged])
```

# Overview

## Row {height="auto"}

::: {.card title="About this dashboard"}

This dashboard shows **how often CanadaLogin users run into errors**, and
whether any error is happening more than usual. It answers questions like
"are we seeing more passkey errors than normal?" It is internal to Enterprise
Digital Credentials and the link is unlisted. For anything that leaves EDCP,
please reach out to the
[Data and Research team](https://gcdigital.slack.com/archives/C0A6S9F7KV4).

**If a "Data quality checks failed" warning appears under the menu bar, a check
failed when the page was made.** Do not quote anything until it clears.

[By Feature](#by-feature) shows errors by the part of CanadaLogin where they
happened, such as passkey setup or sign in. [By Error Code](#by-error-code) shows
the codes that stand out this week, and the busiest ones. Hover over a code to
see its message.

**What is counted.** Every error CanadaLogin reports to Google Analytics, from
the `google_analytics.error_events` table described in the
[metrics cookbook](https://cds-snc.github.io/canadalogin-metrics-cookbook/catalog/google_analytics/error_events.html).
An error is an event, not a failed attempt: someone who mistypes a code three
times counts three times.

**The rate.** Errors per 1,000 sessions across all of CanadaLogin, so a busier
week does not look like a worse one. A feature's rate also rises when more
people use that feature.

**A flag.** A feature or code is flagged when its rate this week is at least
**`r thresholds$ratio` times** the median of the
`r thresholds$history_weeks` weeks before, on at least
**`r thresholds$min_events` errors**. A code is **new** when it had no errors
at all in those `r thresholds$history_weeks` weeks, and **returning** if it
had some in the weeks before them; either is listed once it has at least
`r thresholds$new_min_events` errors in the week. A flag says something changed, not why.

The dashboard is updated every Wednesday and reports the Monday-to-Sunday week
before: Google Analytics runs two days behind.

```{r automated-traffic-note, message=NA}
#| results: asis
# The URL carries a publish token, so it is looked up at render time and the
# note is left out when it cannot be. message=NA sends the reason for a missing
# link to the render log; Quarto's YAML options reject NA.
bot_traffic_url <- published_url("automated-traffic.html")
if (!is.null(bot_traffic_url)) {
  cat(glue("Spikes in sign-up and phone setup errors often come with ",
           "automated traffic. Check the ",
           "[Automated Traffic dashboard]({bot_traffic_url}) for the same ",
           "week.\n"))
}
```

feature_gt(features)

::: {.figure-note}
A feature is the part of CanadaLogin where the error happened, whichever
journey it was part of: passkey setup counts in sign up, password recovery and
account settings alike. Hover over a feature to see the forms it covers.
Each code's bar is its share of the feature's errors.
Hover over a code to see its message.
`r if (length(unlabelled) > 0) glue("Shown by form name, because they have no feature name yet: {glue_collapse(unlabelled, sep = ', ')}.")`

## Row

::: {.card title="Error codes this week"}

```{r codes-table}
if (nrow(codes) == 0) {
  cat("No errors this week.")
} else {
  code_gt(codes)
}
```

::: {.figure-note}
New and returning codes with at least `r thresholds$new_min_events` errors
first, then every other code with at least `r thresholds$list_min_events`
errors this week, most first. Codes are IBM Verify or CanadaLogin
identifiers, shown as Google Analytics records them. Hover over a code to see
its message. *Mostly on* is the feature where the code happened most
this week.
:::
